newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Exim Bank to help fund Chile copper project.
newsitem.headline: Japan Exim Bank to help fund Chile copper project.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Japan and five Japanese banks will provide 18 billion yen ($146 million) in loans to help fund the expansion of Chile's Candelaria copper mine, spokesmen for institutions involved in the deal said on Thursday.
Japan's Sumitomo Metal Mining Co and Sumitomo Corp jointly hold a minority 20 percent stake in the mine, while Phelps Dodge Corp of the United States holds the remainder.
Phelps Dodge announced last May that Candelaria's annual copper output would be expanded in 1998 by 130 million lb to 380 million lb, at a cost of $337 million.
Spokesmen for the Exim Bank and Sumitomo Metal Mining confirmed a report in Thursday's edition of the economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun regarding the financing.
The Exim Bank spokesman said an agreement on the financing was scheduled for signing on Friday and that further details would be made available at that time. --Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-6179
